news_drafts.headline: Denbighshire revised corporate income forecast down by £28.2m to £1.1m and matched cuts to expenditure, keeping overall budget overspend at £510k
news_drafts.lead: Denbighshire Council has revised its corporate income forecast from £29.3m to £1.1m mid-year and made equivalent cuts to expenditure, leaving its net budget position unchanged. The £28.2m reduction in expected income — roughly nine-tenths of what was budgeted — has been matched by spending reductions of the same scale, keeping the council's overall budget overspend at £510k (0.2%) against a total budget of £309m. The adjustment reflects changed circumstances for income sources, though the council has not detailed which. Service-level overspends are modest: Adult Social Care and Homelessness, the largest service budget at £67.8m, is forecast to overspend by £442k; Planning, Public Protection and Countryside by £268k on a £12.2m budget. The overall position has deteriorated by £402k from the previous forecast.
news_drafts.paper_title: FINANCE REPORT - App 1 - Revenue Budget Summary

findings.paper_title: FINANCE REPORT - App 1 - Revenue Budget Summary
findings.headline: Corporate income projections slashed by £28.2m from budgeted £29.3m to £1.1m
findings.detail: Corporate income is now forecast at only £1,077k compared to budgeted £29,271k, a shortfall of £28,194k. This is offset by equivalent expenditure cuts, keeping net position neutral, but the scale of income reduction is extraordinary.
findings.matters: A £28m drop in corporate income expectations signals either loss of expected revenue sources or major budget reclassification; either way, it indicates the council's income base is less stable than budgeted

findings.paper_title: FINANCE REPORT - App 1 - Revenue Budget Summary
findings.headline: Adult Social Care overspending by £442k on the council's largest service budget
findings.detail: Adult Social Care and Homelessness, budgeted at £67,754k (the largest service budget), is forecast to overspend by £442k (0.7%). This is the largest absolute overspend in the services section.
findings.matters: ASC is nationally a growing cost area; overspends here are significant given budget size and reflect sector-wide demand pressures that raise questions about future financial sustainability

findings.paper_title: FINANCE REPORT - App 1 - Revenue Budget Summary
findings.headline: Planning service shows 2.2% overspend, the highest percentage variance across services
findings.detail: Planning, Public Protection and Countryside services are forecast to overspend by £268k against a budget of £12,213k. This is the largest percentage variance in the services section and points to specific cost pressures.
findings.matters: Concentrated overspends in individual services may indicate management control issues or unexpected cost drivers that could spread to other areas

findings.paper_title: FINANCE REPORT - App 1 - Revenue Budget Summary
findings.headline: Council budget overspend of £510k worsens from previous forecast of £108k
findings.detail: Projected Council Budget outturn is £309,415k against budget of £308,905k, a £510k overspend (0.2%). This represents a deterioration of £402k from the previous position. The position is getting worse, not better.
findings.matters: A lender needs to understand trajectory—a deteriorating position suggests budget control is slipping and may require drawing on reserves or immediate corrective action

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - Waste and Recycling Budget and Costs - July 2026
findings.headline: First full year (2025/26) balanced budget rests on £2m Extended Producer Responsibility grant described as uncertain
findings.detail: Service reported balanced budget at 2025/26 year-end: actual costs £8.678m against budget £8.7m. This required £2m pEPR grant funding (out of £2.4m received; £0.4m set aside in reserve). Without grant, costs would have been £10.7m. Council acknowledges future pEPR funding levels are uncertain and whether it will impact Welsh Government's future funding to councils.
findings.matters: Reported balanced budget masks underlying costs of £10.7m that would be unaffordable without continued uncertain grant funding
findings.figures: Reported cost £8.678m; pEPR grant £2m used (£2.4m total received); underlying cost without pEPR £10.7m; budget £8.7m
findings.quote: What is uncertain is how much that funding will be, and whether it impacts in anyway on WG's future funding to Council's in Wales.
